niche_preference_profile: This user prefers clean, airy, highly structured interfaces with strong hierarchy, clear labels, and enough content to feel complete. They like screens that are easy to scan, with separated sections or cards, concise task-focused copy, and explicit controls that make the next action obvious. They generally dislike clutter, oversized hero imagery, overly promotional or verbose text, and layouts that feel sparse, unfinished, or overly modal/overlay-driven. They also show a strong preference for practical, app-like, polished UI with clear affordances and balanced use of space.

criteria.description: Clear title/section hierarchy with obvious focal points and scannable grouping
Open spacing, minimal visual noise, and a lightweight overall composition
Distinct cards or sections that break content into easy-to-scan chunks
Short, direct, practical copy instead of promotional, verbose, or overly explanatory text
Screens that feel populated and finished, with enough visible content and not too much empty space
Controls and rows that clearly show what can be tapped, toggled, or drilled into
Descriptive, scannable labels and headings that make categories and settings easy to understand
Simple headers with limited branding, fewer competing elements, and less top-of-screen clutter
A refined, finished, contemporary interface rather than a generic, system-like, or placeholder feel
Even vertical rhythm and balanced use of the full screen instead of top-heavy or awkwardly sparse layouts
A visible, well-anchored primary CTA that is easy to identify without competing too much with secondary actions
Subtle progress indicators rather than prominent step framing or pagination noise
Interfaces that stay embedded in the task context and show relevant details needed to act immediately
List rows that feel fully formed, with labels, icons, and controls all present and aligned
Avoidance of large decorative hero images or banners that distract from the task
Options presented in a way that explains the choice clearly, such as segmented choices or explanatory rows
One main task flow with fewer competing subheadings, nested layers, or fragmented sections
Obvious back, next, chevron, or overflow affordances that make navigation and drill-down behavior clear
A serious, functional tone that feels task-oriented rather than friendly-marketing or overly casual
Useful contextual specifics like card identity, status, or ending digits when they support the task
